### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **4** documentable anchor(s).

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d96721faac1f0e510b386644fc33b7f4fcbecf8`.

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **15** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d96721faac1f0e510b386644fc33b7f4fcbecf8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a4ee16544cf637ada75a24e8e1a71d38d324c727` — the merge of head `ab5209be3f0b130f44baa86eed77193d2bd4b8a0` into base `6d96721faac1f0e510b386644fc33b7f4fcbecf8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a4ee16544cf637ada75a24e8e1a71d38d324c727 && git checkout a4ee16544cf637ada75a24e8e1a71d38d324c727
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6d96721faac1f0e510b386644fc33b7f4fcbecf8 ab5209be3f0b130f44baa86eed77193d2bd4b8a0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6d96721faac1f0e510b386644fc33b7f4fcbecf8 && git merge --no-ff ab5209be3f0b130f44baa86eed77193d2bd4b8a0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d96721faac1f0e510b386644fc33b7f4fcbecf8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 6d96721faac1f0e510b386644fc33b7f4fcbecf8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ab5209be3f0b130f44baa86eed77193d2bd4b8a0`
Local-runs: none

Read-only review of PR #23353 for card #23226 (ADR-0138 execution card E3, decision D1). Inputs: the card's body and its five comments, the PR body, its four-file list and the net diff against `main` at the head's merge base (`6d96721faa`, which is `origin/main`), the text of ADR-0138 on `main`, and the check-runs on the head. The governing text is D1 and its **Enforced by** paragraph; the row for E3 is quoted on the card. This is a `security` card: the record names doors, functions and steps only.

**Check-runs on the head** (every run completed; last read before this record was posted, 2026-10-14T00:56Z): 41 runs, 35 `success`, 6 `skipped`, 0 red, none still running. The six skipped are the full-battery legs ci.yml's "THE TWO SPEEDS" moves off the `pull_request` path (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, the three Dogfood Regression Gate shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Temporal Conformance) and the opt-in packed-tarball smoke; the `Dogfood Regression Gate` aggregate concludes `success` with zero expected attestations, as that contract says it does on a PR. Consequence for this head: the new dogfood file is **not** CI-exercised before merge; its 13/13 and the 15-file neighbourhood run are the dev's local measurement at `ab5209be3f`, and CI reads it on `main`'s full battery after landing. The unit block runs in Test Core, which is green on the head.

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or public-surface change the diff implies, judged against D1. The code read is step 3.5 of the security middleware in `security-plugin.ts#SecurityPlugin` at the head, the module-level `isGuestEnvelope`, and the two E1 sites that now call it.

1. **A guest insert with no owner (absent, or supplied `null`) is stamped with nothing and the row stays unowned — right.** D1 items 3 and 5. The insert arm takes the stamp only `if (userId)`; the guest envelope (D9: `principalKind: 'guest'`, no `userId`) carries none. The system principal is never written: no code path stands in for the missing id. Ablation leg B (the stamp writing the system principal for a guest) is the negative control, as the PR body reports; leg A cannot red this case because there is no guest-specific code to remove here, and the body says so rather than claiming otherwise.
2. **A guest insert carrying an empty-string owner is normalized to `null`, not stored as `''` and not refused — right.** D1 item 5 says the owner "stays unset". The step already reads `''` as "no owner" for every caller (the stamp arm's own condition, and `isScalarId` names `''` as neither an owner nor an echo), so this applies the step's existing reading to the guest instead of letting a third state land in the anchor. It is a stored-shape narrowing for guest writes only (a signed-in caller's `''` was and is overwritten by the stamp; a non-guest principal without a user id is untouched). No metadata moves. Not a departure from "a guest-supplied owner is refused": an empty string names no owner.
3. **A guest insert carrying a non-empty owner is refused before the self-match and before the transfer grant is consulted — right.** D1 item 3: "A guest-supplied owner is a forgery and is refused." The guest arm precedes `hasTransferGrant()`, so a set carrying `allowTransfer` or `modifyAllRecords` admits nothing for a guest; a non-scalar value (array, object) falls into the same arm and is refused fail-closed. This is the accept-set narrowing the changeset declares: on `main` a guest whose bound set carried the transfer bit stored a forged owner, a real user's id or the system principal's id (the dev's H1 measurement at `bbb9757717`; the reasoning is confirmed by the `main` code order, where the generic forge arm consulted the grant). The anchor tier (`describeAnchorForbiddenBits`) keeps that binding off a production guest, which is why the pins install it through the registry's bare slot (`bindGuest` in the dogfood file) to prove the branch holds on its own, as D1 requires ("whatever it is granted" is the dev's reading of item 2 plus item 3, and the record names no grant that admits a guest's owner).
4. **A guest update that writes `owner_id` — a transfer, a disown or an echo — is refused whatever the grant — right.** The step is D1's named enforcement point for both operations ("stamps an absent `owner_id` … and refuses a forged one"); D1 item 2 makes an echo impossible to be legitimate (the guest owns no row for the pre-image to match) and a disown is an assignment. The guest check sits ahead of `hasTransferGrant()` and of the pre-image read, so no caller-context read is spent on a guest. Negative control in both test files: a signed-in caller holding the transfer grant still transfers the same row.
5. **Signed-in callers are unchanged — right.** The guest arms are reached only when `userId` is absent, and `isGuestEnvelope` requires no user id; the generic refusal's message and conditions are byte-identical to `main`. A non-guest principal with no user id (not a guest envelope) takes exactly the `main` path.
6. **One reader of the guest fact, no new predicate, no public surface — right (H2 held).** `isGuestEnvelope` is module-private (not exported; `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s index is untouched) and restates E1's predicate verbatim. The D3 set-resolution site is rewritten one-to-one; the D4 organization-refusal site is rewritten as its De Morgan complement (`pk !== 'guest' || userId` becomes `!isGuestEnvelope`), truth-table identical. `plugin-sharing`'s module-private `isGuestPrincipal` is a separate function in another package and is not touched, which is correct for this card.
7. **The `publicFormGrant` branch is unchanged — right.** Comment only. The strip of `PUBLIC_FORM_SERVER_MANAGED_FIELDS` (which carries `owner_id` on `main`, `packages/spec/src/security/public-form.ts`) is the form doors' half of D1 and is "enforced today" per the record's enforcement map; a grant context returns from the middleware before step 3.5, so the two halves cannot double-judge one write. `packages/spec` is untouched.
8. **"Supplied" is told from "set by the scenario" by provenance, never by value — right (H3 held).** Confirmed on `main`: the insert path's `triggerHooks('beforeInsert')` runs inside the executor that `executeWithMiddleware` wraps, after the security middleware; a record-change flow is its own write. The pin-2 flow is `runAs: 'system'`, a system write that short-circuits the middleware, which is what D1 item 3 means by the scenario's own writers. One forward fact, not a departure: D1 item 3 also says "the door's declaration may name an owner"; no endpoint declaration key carries an owner today, and when one lands it must write as the scenario, not as the guest's payload, or this branch refuses it. That is the fact for that card. There is no first-class assignment-rule mechanism, so the row's "assignment rule" is pinned through the two writers that exist (hook, flow).
9. **Exemptions unchanged — right.** The `isSystem` short-circuit precedes the step; the `__referentialFieldClear` marker is server-derived and cannot be forged by a guest request.
10. **Refusal shape — right.** The guest refusal reuses `PermissionDeniedError` (`PERMISSION_DENIED`, 403), names no grant to acquire, and carries the prescription (leave the owner out; the object's hooks or flows own the row). A refusal string citing an ADR id has precedent in this file (ADR-0090 D10, ADR-0123 D2), and the doc-authoring gate is green.
11. **Pins against the row — right, each with a negative control.** Unit: `security-plugin.test.ts`, describe `owner_id anchor guard — the guest branch (ADR-0138 D1)` (5 cases: nothing stamped with a member-stamp control; empty owner unset; refused for three grants × three forged owners with the no-owner and member-transfer controls; batch; update). Dogfood: `guest-owner-stamp.dogfood.test.ts`, the four pin describes, through `anonymousCreate`, `expectOwnerRefused`, `storedOwner` and `bindGuest`; the form door pin and its signed-in control; a census of every guest-written row. The census asserts the exact row set, so an extra admitted row (leg A) and a stamped row (leg B) both red it. The PR body's ablation table is consistent with the code read.
12. **Diff footprint — right.** Four files, +622/−2, all in `plugin-security` source and test, one dogfood test, one changeset; the merge commit `ab5209be3f` adds nothing beyond `origin/main`. No governed surface is touched. The PR is from the base repo, not a fork.

### ② Semver level

- **Changeset** `.changeset/23226-guest-owner-stamp.md`: `@objectstack/plugin-security: minor`, a **BREAKING** banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`.
- **Matches the diff — right.** The change is an accept-set narrowing on a runtime value a guest may send; nothing an author can write is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO migration is owed (AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist #3), and the body still states what a guest client does. `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; `major` is refused by `check-changeset-no-major`, so `minor` with the banner plus the disposition is the repo's launch-window convention (recorded in the package CHANGELOGs). The marker's category matches the record row's own disposition for E3, "none: no new key, and nothing moves". The package publishes, so `skip-changeset` does not apply and no label was written. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` are green on the head.
- **`Clause-②:` line — `no (narrowing)`, right.** Nothing refused on `main` is admitted at this head: the `''` owner was admitted on `main` (stored as `''`) and is admitted now (stored as `null`); every other guest-owner write that `main` admitted is now refused. The PR body carries the changeset's line verbatim, and the PR title and the feature commit both carry the `!`.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **`open_questions[0]` — the seed-settle claim re-owns unowned guest-written and form-door rows to the platform admin on each `app:seeded`, departing from D1 items 3 and 5. Escalated, correctly.** The seat answered on the card (comment `6158206845`): filed as #23354, a class (b) finding with option A (narrow the claim to the rows the seed wrote) as the lean, because options B and C conflict with text the record already decided and so are not decision-card options. Judged: the mechanism is `claimSeedOwnershipOnSettle` → `claimSeedOwnership` in `claim-seed-ownership.ts`, outside D1's named enforcement point (the stamp and the `publicFormGrant` branch); none of E3's four pins depends on its answer; the new dogfood fixture declares no seed data and its promotion-time pass precedes every guest write, so its census is not reached by the claim and does not mask the departure. The row is delivered whole, so `Fixes #23226` stands. The dev's choice to continue to a **draft** PR with `needs_decision` instead of a hard stop is right: the departure was outside the stamp, nothing in the diff turns on it, and the PR stayed draft until the seat ruled.
2. **Acceptance note — the class-5 flow door under `runAs: 'system'` bypasses the middleware (this branch included) until D2b's publish refusal lands. Answered: carrier E2.** The record's enforcement map lists "no `system` flow behind an anonymous flow door" under card E2; it is not E3's. The existing dogfood pin for the `runAs: 'user'` refusal is named in the PR body.
3. **Acceptance note — ADR-0138 is cited at every guest-branch site in code but is not in `scripts/adr-anchors/packages__plugins__plugin-security__src__security-plugin.ts.json` (ADR-0055, ADR-0106, ADR-0123 today); "carrier: none". Escalated to the seat as a named follow-up.** Prime Directive #13's corollary (anchor load-bearing spots) applies: the stamp's guest branch is D1's named enforcement point. The per-file registry entry already exists, so the edit is to its `adrs` and `invariant` (a D1 sentence; E1's D3 and D4 sites in the same file are unanchored too and should ride the same edit). `check:adr-anchors` is a presence check over the listed ids and is green on the head; the id is present at all four sites, so the gate's stated purpose (the next author is told which decision they stand on) is met today. Not a blocker on this head, and outside the claim's file surface, which the dev honoured; the seat carries it, either by extending the claim's surface before landing or as its own card.
4. **Deviation — edits beyond step 3.5 (the D3 and D4 reads, a comment in the `publicFormGrant` branch). Answered: within the claimed file, semantics identical (judgment 6).**
5. **Deviation — commit trailers follow AGENTS.md's model-free pair rather than the harness reminder. Answered: right; AGENTS.md outranks the reminder by the reminder's own precedence line.**
6. **Deviations — a temporary probe test file (run once, deleted, never committed) and a build prerequisite for one local gate. Answered: local facts; the diff carries no residue (four files).**
7. **Labels — none written; `skip-changeset` not applied. Right.**
